title: New LSA Method Speeds AI's Full Attention Processing Up to 72.4x
summary:
Researchers have published a new framework called Latent Sparse Attention to optimize how artificial intelligence models handle ultra-long context windows without sacrificing accuracy. The LSA method reduces the computational burden of the attention mechanism, providing a processing boost of up to 22.7x for sparse attention and 72.4x for full attention.

The open research release targets a specific efficiency bottleneck in large scale processing; the team noted that when handling 10M tokens, the search for relevant tokens accounts for 98% of an attention layer's time. By implementing subquadratic attention, the researchers intend to allow models to scale their context windows more efficiently.

selectedTweets.text:
Today we are happy to share one of our first open research releases: Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), a step towards subquadratic attention that matches accuracy of full attention at ultra-long context.

Sparse attention attends to only a few tokens per query, but it has to find the right ones. At 10M tokens, that search takes 98% of the attention layer's time. LSA makes sparse attention up to 22.7× faster and full attention 72.4x faster.

With @kubicek_ales @caciolai @PengLiangzu @SukritSumant @Ben_Hoov @FraserGreenlee @RMBattleday @radim_urban @thoefler @jcrwhittington
